title: Module Re-exports
story: Your utils module has submodules `parser`, `formatter`, and `validator` - each with their own public functions. Users shouldn't need to type `utils.parser.parse` and `utils.formatter.format`. You want a clean API: just `utils.parse` and `utils.format`. Re-exports make this possible.
why: Re-exports (`pub use`) let you organize internal module structure however you want while presenting a clean, flat public API to users.
analogy: A department store has stock rooms organized by category (submodules) but the sales floor (public API) arranges items by what customers want to find. Re-exports are the store clerks who bring items from the back room to the front shelf.
try_it: Design a `game` module with submodules `player`, `enemy`, and `world`. Each has 2-3 pub functions. Use re-exports to create a clean flat API: `game.spawn_player()`, `game.spawn_enemy()`, `game.generate_world()`. Hide the submodule structure.
tips: `pub use sub::func;` both re-exports AND makes it public at the new level
Re-exports let you reorganize internal code without breaking users
Use `as` to rename: `pub use sub::func as better_name;`
common_mistakes: Using `use sub::func;` without `pub` - the item stays private in the parent
Re-exporting everything indiscriminately - still curate your public API
Forgetting that re-exported items still need the original to be `pub`
